summary: Retires the IETF's old FTP service by updating older RFCs that pointed to it. This document replaces the FTP-based links found in affected IETF and IAB stream RFCs with HTTPS links so the referenced material can still be found. It is a housekeeping change and does not alter any protocol.

eli5.summary: A library closes an old door, so this note tells everyone which new door to use to reach the same books.

questions: why was the ietf ftp service retired
what replaced ftp.ietf.org links in rfcs
subtitle: Replaces dead ftp:// links to the IETF FTP service in older RFCs with HTTPS links to the same material.

tldr.problem: The IETF FTP service at ftp.ietf.org, ops.ietf.org and ietf.org is being retired, but a number of published RFCs contain URIs that point to it.
tldr.mechanism: This document updates each affected RFC with OLD and NEW text, swapping the ftp:// URIs for HTTPS URIs, and gives a generic rule for any other RFC with an ftp://ftp.ietf.org/ reference.
tldr.outcome: The referenced material stays findable, and the links now use HTTPS instead of cleartext FTP. No protocol changes.

facts.label: Generic replacement
facts.value: https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/ followed by the old path

today: RFC 9141 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2021 and has not been obsoleted or updated. It is the reference for the replacement text in the RFCs it updates, such as RFC 2418 and RFC 4251.

sections.title: Why the FTP References Must Change
sections.content:
After community consultation in late 2020, it was decided to retire the IETF FTP service running at ftp.ietf.org, ops.ietf.org and ietf.org. An appendix of the retirement plan identifies 30 RFCs, published in the IETF and IAB streams between 1997 and 2006, that have at least one explicit or inline reference to a URI pointing to that service.

To keep the referenced materials findable, this document formally updates those RFCs that had not already been updated by other documents, replacing the FTP URIs with HTTPS URIs to the same materials. Published RFCs are not edited in place, so an update document like this one is the way to correct them.
sections.eli5: Some old notes say to look for a book in a room that is closing. This note says which new room to go to instead.

sections.title: How the Updates Are Written
sections.content:
Section 3 goes through each affected RFC. The original text is quoted with OLD and the replacement text with NEW, so a reader can see exactly what changes. Requirements words such as MUST are used as defined in BCP 14.

The RFCs updated are 2077, 2418, 2648, 2954, 2955, 3020, 3083, 3201, 3202, 3295, 3684, 3962, 3970, 4036, 4131, 4251, 4323, 4546, 4547, 4639, 4682, 5098 and 5428. Additionally, with permission of the IAB, RFC 6756 and RFC 7241 are also updated.
sections.eli5: Each fix is shown as a before and after, like crossing out an old address on a letter and writing the new one beside it.

sections.title: The Kinds of References Replaced
sections.content:
Most of the changes fall into a few patterns:

  • Mailing list archives in MIB contact info. Many MIB modules carry an Email Archive or Archive line in their CONTACT-INFO, such as ftp://ftp.ietf.org/ietf-mail-archive/ipcdn. The new form is https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/ietf-mail-archive/ipcdn/. RFC 3970 pointed at ftp://ops.ietf.org/pub/lists and now points at https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/concluded-wg-ietf-mail-archive/tewg/.
  • Informative references to specific emails. RFC 3684, RFC 3962 and RFC 4251 cite individual messages in the mail archive, and those citations get the same kind of HTTPS replacement.
  • Lists of RFCs and Internet-Drafts. RFC 2077, RFC 6756 and RFC 7241 pointed at copies of RFCs and Internet-Drafts or at index files. The new locations are https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/ for RFCs and https://www.ietf.org/id/ for Internet-Drafts.
  • Meeting minutes. RFC 2648 treats the subtree at ftp://ietf.org/ietf/ as the definitive assignment of URNs for working group minutes. It now points at https://www.ietf.org/how/meetings/proceedings/. The scripts in its Appendix A are not updated.
sections.eli5: Most of the fixes are address changes for the places where old emails and document lists are kept.

sections.title: The Generic Rule
sections.content:
The RFC also covers references it did not list. If any other RFC not explicitly mentioned contains a reference of the form ftp://ftp.ietf.org/<path>, the reference MUST be replaced with a URI of the form https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/<path>.

In practice this means readers who meet an old FTP link in an RFC can rewrite it mechanically by swapping the scheme and host prefix and keeping the path.
sections.eli5: If you find an old address that was not on the list, there is a simple rule for turning it into the new address.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
This document does not alter the security considerations of the updated documents. It replaces URIs to IETF infrastructure that use the FTP scheme with equivalent HTTPS URIs, which keeps the referenced content available after the FTP service is retired.

Replacing cleartext FTP with HTTPS also lets resources be reached more securely. HTTPS provides an encrypted channel with server identity verification through the client's certificate checking, plus integrity and confidentiality protection that match the negotiated TLS version and cipher suite. This document has no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: The new doors have locks that the old ones lacked, so visitors are safer, and the library asked for nothing from the city office.
